headline: Public Law 114-5 directs Congress to present gold medals to the Foot Soldiers who took part in the 1965 Selma to Montgomery voting rights marches.
what_it_does: The law tells the Speaker of the House and the President Pro Tempore of the Senate to arrange a Congressional Gold Medal presentation on Congress's behalf. The medal honors people who marched in Bloody Sunday, Turnaround Tuesday, or the final Selma to Montgomery march in March 1965. The law says the medals are national medals.
when_it_takes_effect: Upon enactment on March 7, 2015, since the summary gives no later date.
